Translation into 中文-普通话 國語 available: 【授权翻译】别浪费你的感情（倾心于我） Don't go wasting your emotion (lay all your love on me) by min_tac When the first blood stained white petal fell from his mouth, Phainon knew he was screwed, no, doomed. He'd been feeling off all week and now here he was in the school bathroom, trying to scrub the drops of blood off the bathroom sink with a sorry excuse for a tissue paper. It vaguely felt like he was cleaning up a crime scene.

The crime being his feelings for Mydei- the co- class president, captain of the sports team ,his rival and his best friend.

Brilliant.

It's not like he asked to fall so hard for his golden eyed rival. It kind of just… happened. One day, Mydei seemed to shine more than he usually did and then his presence itself made Phainon's heart rate spike to an unnatural extent and all Phainon could think of was Mydei every time they came into contact. Even then, it's not like Phainon's behaviour around Mydei changed a lot once he spent that one night sitting in the bathroom, mentally bashing himself over being so stupid as to fall for Mydei. They were still Mydei and Phainon, Phainon and Mydei. Competitors slash friends.

Their fellow students loved the rivalry between Mydei and Phainon, each forming their separate teams on who to support. Mydei called it stupid, scowling his signature 'death scowl' (Phainon dubbed it that, much to Mydei's chagrin) every time some student placed a bet on who would win the next contest. Phainon reveled in the attention, for it seemed that the student body loved him. He was someone who craved attention and thrill of validation like it was sustenance. To be loved and admired from a distance made him feel most like himself.

It didn't entirely fix the gaping void in his heart, the one that yearned for someone to see behind the precariously crafted facade of 'Phainon'. Someone he could drop the smile around and cry in front of. This hypothetical someone should always remain a distant wish, for Phainon did not truly deserve someone like that. He must give all of himself, and even then, that person would find a way to give him even more and he'd feel indebted to them.

But you take what you get and you don't complain, even if the stares of expectation feel like nails stabbed into your body. Even if the sting of loneliness feels like a dull ache in the back of your throat, threatening to choke you.

He was choking at that very moment, matter of fact, but it was the stupid petals that had lodged themselves in his throat. And it was all Mydei's fault.

He wanted to throttle and kiss Mydei at the same time.

Phainon gagged as he extracted one last petal from the roof of his mouth.His heart was hammering in his chest. Emotions that he thought he'd successfully suppressed and locked up were threatening to surge and devour him. He hadn't felt afraid in a long, long time and now, fear might just topple his house of cards.

He didn't want to think about his inevitable fate. Bloody flower petals meant Hanahaki disease and Hanahaki disease meant he was running out of time. He'd die of his unrequited love for Mydei or get surgery to completely forget about his feelings for the boy with the pretty gold eyes. Some selfish part of Phainon wanted to cling onto his feelings for Mydei, even if he would never look his way. It's not like he had the money to get the surgery, so was he just going to have to weather it out? Quite possibly. Just then, the bell rang, signaling the start of morning classes.

He straightened his tie, extra tight around his throat to look more put together, trying to distract himself from the tinny smell of iron. Externally, he was glowing. Internally? He was crumbling faster than his self respect when it came to Mydei.

He sauntered out of the bathroom as if he hadn't just been throwing up flower petals and having a mental breakdown a while ago. He popped his head into the classroom and his gaze immediately locked in on Mydei. Mydei sat near the window, reading a book, his strawberry blonde hair with red tips obscuring most of his face. Mydei was gorgeous- no, he was the reason why the word gorgeous was invented. He was tall and well built with a face that Phainon would go do unspeakable things for.

Never mind, Phainon wanted to brush the hair from his face tenderly and kiss him at the same time.

Phainon made his way over to Mydei and placed a hand on Mydei's chair, leaning over to see what Mydei was so engrossed in.

"Well, hello there, Mydei" Phainon greeted him cheerfully "Is that a Kremnoan history book?"

Mydei gave a noncommittal grunt as his response. Classic.

"The student council meeting will be at lunch. You'd better be there." Mydei said, finally looking up. Phainon could have sworn he ascended on the spot as Mydei locked eyes with him.

Phainon was a weak man to those eyes.

"Of course!" He chirped, finding his voice so that he wouldn't have to nod dumbly.

He flopped onto his seat, his mind screaming at him to act normal- whatever normal meant for him, at least.

He wasn't so sure of himself anymore.

✧ 𖥔 ݁ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑☀️𖥔 ݁ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑ ✧

As classes progressed, Phainon found it increasingly difficult to concentrate. His lungs felt constricted, the burn of the flowers making him feel restless. His head felt fuzzy, like it was stuffed with cotton, or maybe flowers, in Phainon's case. That joke should've made him laugh or at least crack a smile. Instead, it had the opposite effect, ringing in his head like a reminder that he was utterly, horribly screwed. When the time came to converse with his classmates and do his duties as class president, he smiled like he was programmed to do and did his best to be everyone's friend. He was Phainon, after all. Phainon never, never acted like anything was wrong. When his parents died when he was in middle school, Phainon sucked it up and showed up for the sports meet because he couldn't stand disappointing his teammates. He can still remember crying in the shower after they won the game, head throbbing and feeling feverish as he leaned against the cool tile.

In sixth period, he absentmindedly doodled chimeras with what little artistic talent he had on some loose sheets of paper. He was working on one when the bell for lunch rang. Unfortunately, he didn't notice the figure looming over his paper before it was too late.

"Deliverer, those chimeras look like they've been dropped in a vat of acid. Are you sure this isn't a cry for help?" Mydei asked, using that annoying nickname he'd sourced from a character in a series who he thought resembled Phainon.

"I- huh? What-" Phainon scrambled to hide the offending doodles and looked up at Mydei, somewhat alarmed. He wanted to curl up into a ball, disintegrate and be scattered by the wind.

"…"

Mydei scrutinized him for a minute before nodding in the direction of the Student Council room.

Oh. That.

Phainon trailed after him, eyes fixated on Mydei's blonde hair, itching to run his hands through it and maybe even braid it. As they walked, Phainon made sure to keep an endless stream of chatter with Mydei- talking about anything and everything while Mydei listened. It was a routine they'd fallen into since they were freshmen- Mydei listened and Phainon talked. Other times, they'd bicker and compete. It was safe, easy and familiar.

Aglaea, a senior and the head of the Student Council sat at the head of the table. She made the average high school senior look like a malformed bug in comparison to her. Top of the class, head of the Student Council and high profile designer in the making, Aglaea had it all. Seated opposite to her was the infamous Anaxa. He insisted that everyone call him Anaxagoras, but most people called him Anaxa, much to his annoyance. Part of the student council as head of the chemistry club (he insisted that it was the alchemy club), he and Aglaea weren't exactly on the best terms, just to put wanting to strangle each other nicely.

Castorice, a fellow junior who was in a different class, sat hunched over a notebook she always carried around. Phainon had tried to ask about the notebook's contents, but Castorice would shake her head and refuse to elaborate. She was the president of the art club, so he assumed that the notebook was filled with sketches she was too shy to show.

Mydei and Phainon slid into their seats next to each other- inseparable in a way Phainon used to be with Cyrene. Both of them were worthy candidates for the sports captain and class president, so they were told to team up for both.

"Hi, Cas! What are you drawing?" Phainon asked, trying to ignore the pain in his cheeks from smiling so much that day

"Oh. Uh, nothing" Castorice looked at the table, seeming very interested in following the cracks that lined the table. Her reaction reminded him of his own reactions to Mydei judging his doodles earlier. Although, Phainon could've sworn he saw a hand cupping someone else's face.

"Ah, Hyacine, good that you're here" Aglaea's voice cut through the air, snapping him out of his thoughts.

The bubblegum haired sophomore pushed open the door and waved at the Council. Phainon grinned and waved back at her.

"Alright, I have the documents for the sports fest this year. The refreshments and sports equipment have been accounted for." Hyacine read off a list

"Perfect. Phainon, Mydei, you two know the drill. Handle the selections and organise the events. I trust that you two will have this under control, yes?" Aglaea inquired

Phainon nodded eagerly, doing his best to not think of having to spend even more time with Mydei than he already did and risk getting his Hanahaki discovered.

"Yep! You can count on us"

"Yes" was all Mydei said.

Phainon could feel the flower petals rising in his lungs. Up till now, he'd just dealt with the discomfort of the petals, but now, he felt as though he might throw up. He stood up as calmly as he could considering he was seconds away from coughing up bloodied petals.

"I need to use the bathroom. See you guys later." Phainon announced in his most convincing happy voice he could muster and booked it out of the room. He didn't notice Mydei's concerned expression, having realised something was off.

✧ 𖥔 ݁ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑☀️𖥔 ݁ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑ ✧

It was getting worse. He coughed up even more flower petals than earlier in the morning, feeling horrible- not unlike trash on the side of the road. Phainon wiped his mouth and splashed some water on his face, trying to gaslight himself into thinking he's totally, one hundred percent fine. Yep, Nothing wrong.

"Did you just cough up a flower?"

Oh shit.

Phainon turned around slowly on his heel, like one of those scenes in horror movies where the protagonist goes he's right behind me isn't he? There was, in fact, a perplexed, no, concerned- Phainon couldn't pinpoint the emotion because of the eye patch covering one eye-Anaxa facing him. It was a rookie mistake, choosing to throw up in front of the sink.

"Uhh- no?" He stammered out "No. That was a flower. I'm certain you just regurgitated a flower. You've either eaten the flowers in the garden Hyacine tends to or you have Hanahaki."

God damn it.

"Who is it then? The person you're pining after?"

"… nobody"

Phainon felt like he was being flayed open, like a specimen in a lab. Better yet, he felt like the frog he and Mydei dissected earlier that week in biology, its organs lined up neatly next to it the time they were done. He decided that he hated this feeling.

"You can't just expect me to believe you've fallen in love with a ghost." Anaxa paused, mulling over something before continuing with his thorough dissection of Phainon with his words."It's Mydeimos, isn't it?"

It sounded less like a question and more like a statement. Knowing Anaxa, it would be futile to argue.

"Yes."

Anaxa didn't even have the decency to act surprised. He just nodded like that was just a backing to his already correct assumptions.

"Now, you have two options- either confess your feelings to him and have him return them or get surgery. I'm sure you know about the consequences of not doing either."

Phainon, in the middle of his confusion and distress, wanted to laugh. Mydei, like him back? That was one of the most ridiculous statements he had ever heard. So the first option was crossed off in his mind instantly. He didn't even have the money for the surgery- the only reason he could attend Okhema High was because of the scholarship that covered his living expenses as well as his tuition. Long story short, he was flat broke. Anaxa's uncovered eye bore into his soul, expecting an answer.

Oh Kephale, this was bad. It's not like he could just stop loving Mydei, not when every little interaction with Mydei made him fall for him all over again.

It was at this very moment that an idea struck him. He'd always been one for insane, often diabolical ideas, but this one took the cake.

What if he became Mydei's enemy and then got himself to hate Mydei so that the spread of the Hanahaki would stop and he'd fall out of love and get cured? It was an insane idea, yes. Did Phainon have serious attachment issues? Also yes. Did Phainon feel unworthy of being near Mydei- unworthy of loving him? Unfortunately, yes.

Even then, Phainon's confusion and fear addled brain decided that this would be the best course of action.

"Anaxa?"

"For the umpteenth time, it's Anaxagoras, you fool."

"Sorry, sorry- I won't do it again, Anaxa. Wait. Oh—"

"Forget it." Anaxa said delicately, barely concealing his murderous intent.

"Right. This is a hypothetical situation, okay? What if a person with Hanahaki started to hate the person they initially fell for? Would it possibly cure them?"

Anaxa narrowed his eyes but decided to play along.

"In theory, yes. Hate can cancel out love. However, it would take a different breed of a self - sabotaging moron to actually do that, though. Not when the best alternative is to get surgery."

Phainon chose to ignore the pointed look Anaxa was throwing at him. Anaxa wouldn't be able to understand- he wasn't desperate like Phainon was. He would never know what it was like to secretly take up jobs to have enough for his personal expenses, to be someone who had to come to school with a sunny, dependable smile and act like he didn't fail to pay the electricity bills for that month. Anaxa probably never knew what it felt like to be alone and so used to that hollow, all encompassing loneliness that losing another loved one was inevitable to him.

Mydei would leave Phainon eventually. He was everything Phainon would never be. The heir of Kremnos Industries, with a future as bright as he was. Mydei could fall any time, because someone would always catch him and hug him and tell him it was alright. Phainon couldn't afford to fall. To fail was to plunge into the abyss and have to scrape the bits of blood off his fingernails from trying too hard to hold on.

Mydei was a good thing and Phainon couldn't have good things.

"I'll think about it." was all Phainon could muster before heading out of the bathroom.

✧ 𖥔 ݁ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑☀️𖥔 ݁ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑ ✧

So began Phainon's elaborate plan of self sabotage. Was he going to destroy the best friendship he's ever had? Yes.

Phainon had begged the Mydei in his head for forgiveness over and over again. In his mind's eye, he had keeled onto the floor as he held Mydei's hand and cried, whispering apologies. Bringing his head to the floor, he'd crumpled in a ball and wished he never fell for Mydei to begin with- cursing himself for being so selfish. He'd then looked up at Mydei and pleaded for him to understand why he was doing what he was. He hated the thought that Mydei would be hurt by his own stupidity. This was probably reason number forty five why he hated himself as much as he did. Yes, he did indeed have a list, but that's besides the point.

He began to avoid Mydei like the plague, which was easier said than done, considering the fact that they were partnered up for everything from class presidency to organising the sports meet. In the end, he opted to stop talking and making eye contact with Mydei, It killed him to see Mydei look up expectantly when Phainon entered the classroom only to watch as Phainon walked right by him without so much as a glance. When Mydei would approach him for something that wasn't related to the sports meet or the class, Phainon would get up and walk away.

The past two weeks of Phainon's life were a mess. He missed Mydei terribly, to his own fault, he reminded himself as he blocked Mydei's number (my day mouse, it said- he was particularly proud of that name). Each day was a struggle as number of white petals he coughed up increased.

Brilliant.

Now Phainon was broke, miserable and Mydei- less(A term he came up while trying to describe the pit in his stomach and the emptiness in the air that surrounded him)

The rest of the student council had noticed the duo separated and Phainon was questioned about this new development a few times. Cipher had asked him if they were in the midst of a lover's quarrel, which Phainon shut down as quickly as he could. The other students had caught on to the fact that the two weren't talking anymore as well. Rumors floated around all the time, some of which Phainon was unfortunate enough to stumble upon.

"They must've broken up!"

"But I don't think they were dating"

"Then they must've fought!"

"But what kind of fight could drive those two apart?"

Phainon did his best to appear unbothered as he walked by the group, his head held high.

Mydei seemed to have decided to talk it out with Phainon and corner him at any chance he got. Phainon would ignore Mydei if he broached the topic of them not speaking as they prepared for the sports meet. He'd refuse to talk about anything else on purpose. Each time, Mydei would groan in frustration and eventually give up on trying to pry answers from Phainon's sealed lips. On other duty unrelated situations, he found creative ways to avoid Mydei. Creative by his definition, at least.

Which is how they ended up sprinting through the halls at 8 in the morning.

"Get back here, HKS. I need answers!" Mydei yelled as he chased Phainon down the stairs.

"I'm sorry! It's not you, it's me!"

"The hell do you mean?"

"I messed up and now I- ugh- I can't do this right now! I'm running!"

"Then stop running!"

"Then stop chasing me!"

It was Phainon's fault for bumping into the homeroom teacher at that very moment because the next thing he knew, he and Mydei were sentenced to detention. Really, as class presidents and sports captains, you should be ashamed of yourselves, the teacher had berated them before allowing them into the class. The day slugged by, Phainon trying to be as inconspicuous with his periodic visits to cough out lungfuls of petals.

Phainon got to the detention room first and collapsed on a chair near the window. He was exhausted and had been for a while now. He slouched and pulled the hood of his jacket up, wishing the floor would swallow him up.

"Phainon?" Castorice's voice came from behind the door as it creaked open. She must've passed by and spotted him

"You're here because of the detention you and Mydei got for running in the halls and causing a ruckus, aren't you?"

"Yeah."

"What.. happened? It's not like you two to just stop talking to each other like that. You're too close to ever do that."

Phainon wanted to confess everything, wanted to finally tell someone the bitter pain he'd been forcing himself to swallow over and over again.

On the first day of the plan, Phainon had written down four simple steps to make Mydei hate him-

Step 1: avoid him

Step 2: tell people you hate him; express that you think of him as your enemy

Step 3: watch as he hates you and stops trying to figure out what's wrong.

Step 4: lose your feelings for him and cure yourself of your Hanahaki

He'd accomplished step 1, so it should be time to begin with step 2 - telling people he hated Mydei.

"Mydei and I, we can't be friends, Cas. We're too different. He's a rich heir with all the money in the world and I'm nothing at all. I just- I just hung out with him because it was convenient for me. I don't actually like him. I just happened to gain some dignity and decide to leave him."

Phainon could not believe the words coming out of his own mouth. He regretted every last word he said, but he was too far in it now. It was like the voice he heard wasn't really his and the real Phainon was somewhere in his mind, slamming the floor and beseeching him to stop talking.

Midway through his tirade, Castorice looked like she was about to say something and then startled, gawking at the door. Phainon belatedly realised why she looked so alarmed.

There he was, as radiant as ever. Mydeimos, standing at the door, his jaw set, eyebrows scrunched and looking the closest thing to heartbroken as Phainon's ever seen.

Phainon had never hated himself more than he did in that moment.

"Go. Follow him" Castorice urged, looking more angry and distressed than Phainon had ever seen her. Hell, he'd thought that the mild mannered Castorice was incapable of feeling anger up until that point.

Phainon's mind was a jumbled mess of whatthehelldidyoudoyouidiot and ihateyouihateyouihateyou reverberating through his skull. His heart felt like it was throbbing against his ribcage as he rounded a corner in the school garden where he and Mydei liked to play fight. Mydei was already standing there, the golden eyes that reminded him of the blazing sun meeting his own.

"…Phainon"

That was the one of the rare times Mydei had called Phainon by his name. In any other situation, he would have savoured the moment and held it close to his heart and never let go. Just not in this one, because Mydei's voice was the only thing he could hear apart from the TV static buzzing in his mind.

"A rich heir with all the money in the world. Is that all you see me as? A convenience? Someone you just stuck around with and never even saw as a friend?"

"No- I-"

"Phainon. Please. Don't lie. Tell me, what did these two years mean to you?"

"That wasn't what I meant- I didn't mean to phrase it like that. It was just the situation, the wrong thing slipped out and- oh Kephale, I have no excuses. I mean, look at you and look at me. What would any rational person think when they see us side- by - side? The heir of Kremnos Industries next to some charity case of a country boy- that's what they'd see." Phainon spat the words out like they were acid on his tongue, acid he'd inevitably spew.

Phainon must have imagined the flicker of pain in Mydei's eyes, like he was wishing this was all a bad dream. There was a long pause in which Phainon was certain he'd done it- pushed away yet another person he loved. This is for the best, a voice in his head whispered, you wanted this, you wanted to make him hate you. Finally, Mydei spoke, in a voice that lacked his usual quiet confidence- hell, he looked hurt.

"Since when have you ever been lesser than I?"

Phainon felt sick to his stomach. A wave of nausea threatened to crawl up his stomach and his throat felt like it was being crushed. (Maybe that was the stupid flowers, Phainon hoped he didn't start coughing them up right then and there) Why didn't Mydei hate him yet? Why was Mydei hurt instead of angry? Phainon wanted to say something to placate Mydei, but he knew he would recognise his lies as though Phainon was made out of see- through glass.

When Phainon stared mutely at Mydei, Mydei scoffed - not derisively, but defeatedly. He must have understood the meaning of his silence.

I am not and never will be an equal to you.

"So be it. Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, you were the first person who could best me. I was foolish to believe you thought of me the way I do you."

A pause

"Goodbye."

With that, Mydei walked away, leaving Phainon clutching at his shattered heart. His lungs burned as he ducked behind a wall and coughed up a whole, bloodstained lily.

✧ 𖥔 ݁ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑☀️𖥔 ݁ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑ ✧

It had been a day since the incident. Mydei, true to his word, didn't so much as look at Phainon the entire rest of the day. Phainon felt despondent as he trudged back into the small flat the scholarship had provided him with. On Saturday. his phone buzzed with a reminder for Tuesday's meeting with Mydei to finalise some details for the sports meet. He had no idea how he was going to face Mydei again after what he said and did. Phainon spent the entire day moping and occasionally crying as he made himself instant noodles because that was all he knew to make. He was a wreck, to put it lightly. His phone did occasionally buzz with texts from Castorice asking if he was alright, all of which he felt guilty for ignoring.

Lilies tore out of Phainon's lungs as he hunched over the toilet, the flower's smooth petals akin to sandpaper. The steady dripping of blood into the toilet bowl was the thing he chose to focus on to ground himself.

Phainon was certain he was going to die. Of his feelings for Mydei, no less.

It seemed as though the plan to make Mydei hate him and to grow to become his enemy had failed miserably. The only person he could bring himself to hate was himself. He made a mental note to never, ever make plots of any shape or form ever again.

Monday rolled around and Phainon knew that no amount of pep talks or gas-lighting himself to think everything was fine would fix the mess he made. Mydei did show up that day, albeit a bit delayed, which was strange considering his stellar reputation for being punctual. Phainon's day felt like a fever dream; he chatted and laughed and smiled until his cheeks hurt, but he didn't remember much else. After school, he decided to find Castorice and apologise for involving her in the mess and dismissing her concern.

Man, he felt like such a bad friend.

He got to the art club, but her seat was empty. He was about to turn around and search for her elsewhere, but her sketchbook caught his eye. In his defense, the sketchbook was open and covered only by a pencil pouch. Maybe he was so out of it that common decency evaded him, but he moved the pencil pouch aside to peer into the book.

In front of him lay sketches of him and Mydei. That wouldn't be a problem if not for the less than platonic way in which they held each other. A flush crept up his cheeks and ears.

Well, at least Phainon now knew whose hands were cupping whose face.

A strangled gasp brought him out of his thoughts. Castorice looked like she would give anything to yeet herself out the window and into the bushes below.

"Oh- I- I'm so sorry, I don't know what came over me" Phainon tried to piece together an apology that would make him sound less like an asshole.

"No- did you see any of that?"

"Yes, but I swear I didn't mean too. Promise, Cas."

A long pause followed. Castorice was the first to break it.

"Do you hate me now?"
